chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan [al-Husayn] ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
What is wrong with you? Why do you not go to him? – This refers to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Verily, four thousand angels cry [weep for him] by his grave until the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims visit the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the cosmological significance of Karbala, portraying Imam al-Husayn’s grave as a focal point of divine mercy where four thousand angels maintain perpetual weeping until the Resurrection. It reflects the Shia tradition of viewing the Ahl al-Bayt’s shrines not merely as historical sites but as active spiritual centers where the celestial and earthly realms intersect through continuous worship.
